assertion.statement: For the actual primitive chi_h used in the current retained-class calculation, replacing its Gauss basis by sqrt(h)e_chi costs only the fixed factor ±1 or ±2 and no factor depending on the number of odd conductor primes.
assertion.objects: The primitive quadratic character, its finite Gauss sum, and the chosen square root of odd squarefree signed h.
assertion.hypotheses: Primitivity at the actual conductor; the signed fundamental discriminant convention Delta_h in {h,4h}; chi_h(-1)=sign(Delta_h); the quadratic action on sqrt(h).
assertion.quantifiers: Every such fixed character; the trivial conductor-one character is treated separately.
assertion.parameter_range: All signed odd squarefree h in this convention, including the discriminant4h case.
assertion.uniformity: The possible basis ratios form the fixed set {1,-1,2,-2}.
assertion.normalizations: tau=sum_x chi(x) exp(2*pi*i*x/D), chi extended by zero; no normalized average.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No positive Gauss-sum sign is claimed; D=1 has tau=1.
assertion.limit_order: Finite sums only; no coefficient or cyclotomic inverse limit.

use.reason: Apply the finite-character proof to the actual primitive quadratic character and its signed fundamental discriminant. Both tau and sqrt(h) transform by chi_h; their tensor products with e_chi are invariant. The ratio conclusion is only up to sign, exactly as needed here. The actual character/discriminant identification is retained as a caller condition, not deduced from Fourier orthogonality.
use.shared_contract_justification: Both occurrences concern the identical primitive character, original invariant line and signed discriminant normalization; the second explicitly repeats the same basis calculation.

supplier.statement: For a primitive quadratic character of conductor D, tau squared equals chi(-1)D and sigma_a(tau)=chi(a)tau. Under the stated signed fundamental-discriminant convention, tau/sqrt(h) belongs to {1,-1,2,-2}.
